items.X_name: Construction and its validity range derived, not tuned
items.X_desc: For posts that hinge on an explicit construction (a triple, a family, a substitution, a witness sequence), score jointly (a) whether the post shows where the construction comes from and (b) whether the range over which it works is established algebraically. 10: the construction is solved for out of the conditions it must satisfy (set up the required equations, invert them to get the object), and the range of parameters is derived by an explicit inequality or covering argument. 5: one of the two halves is done (derived object with hand-checked range, or conjured object with derived range). 0: the object appears from nowhere ('consider the triple ...', 'I claim these numbers work') and its applicability is patched by hand-listed numeric special cases or a single verified instance.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when a parameterized construction is accompanied by a proof that its valid parameter ranges cover every permitted instance; score 0 when it supplies only examples or asserts coverage without closing the gaps.

items.X_desc: Score 10 when each nontrivial inference is supported by an equation, construction, or stated reason that an independent reader can check; score 0 when key steps are asserted with phrases such as “obvious,” “clearly,” or “it follows” without support.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the argument is decomposed into multiple separately labeled claims (e.g., 'Claim 1,' 'Claim 2'), each accompanied by its own proof or justification. Score 0 if the argument is a single monolithic block or has no identifiable intermediate assertions.

items.X_desc: Score 10 when the post identifies a quantity or state relation preserved or decreasing under every move, handles ties or exceptional transitions, and explains termination; score 0 when it merely names a monovariant without proving those properties.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when the post derives a compact invariant, normal form, or structural reformulation tailored to the problem; score 0 when it only performs isolated substitutions or calculations without exposing structure.

items.X_name: Asserts a solution versus queries or corrects one
items.X_desc: Score the speech act of the post. 10 = the post advances its own argument and stands behind it, ending in a stated answer or a QED. 0 = the post's actual purpose is to ask a question or to contest someone else - 'Can someone please explain why 391 is incorrect?', 'I am confused on the wiki solution #2 for this ... Wouldn't that be overcounting?', '@above that is listing everything out ... 7/20 is not .7' - even when a complete and well-written derivation is embedded inside the post. Score the framing, not the embedded mathematics.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the solution contains multiple explicitly labeled claims or lemmas (using 'Claim:', 'Lemma:', or equivalent markers), each with its own proof block. Score 0 if the solution is unstructured flowing prose or raw calculations with no organizational markers.

items.X_name: Direct proof of problem as stated, without strengthening
items.X_desc: Score 10 if the solution proves exactly the statement asked without first establishing a materially stronger or generalized result. Score 0 if the solution explicitly or implicitly proves a strengthened version that goes beyond what the problem requires.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the solution is presented as definitive and correct without hedging, doubt, or appeals for validation. Score 0 if the post expresses uncertainty, asks if the approach is valid, or indicates the solver gave up.

items.X_name: Load-bearing guess or approximation, patched afterwards
items.X_desc: Score whether the decisive step is an unmotivated guess or a numerical approximation that the post then tries to justify. 10 = every decisive step is deduced; nothing is assumed and later checked. 0 = the post writes something like 'let a^2 = ab = b^2 since a and b differ by only 2, thus a^2 = 5184.3' and then locates the answer by proximity, or 'assume that the points form a right angle at (1,2)' and then verifies that assumption by substitution. Mid scores when a guess is made but the verification is complete and the guess is clearly signposted as a shortcut.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the post explicitly verifies that all proposed solutions/candidates actually satisfy the original problem conditions (e.g., 'All three clearly work,' or direct substitution back). Score 0 if candidates are proposed without any verification.

items.X_desc: Score whether the post states a single crisp pivotal identity, lemma, or structural fact as a self-contained claim that could stand alone as the crux of a solution, independent of whether surrounding derivation or final computation is completed. A 10: a specific formula/identity/lemma is explicitly isolated and named as the key fact (e.g., stated on its own line or flagged as 'the key point is...'), even if little else is derived. A 0: no such isolable pivotal fact ever appears; the post is either a diffuse mass of computation with no single fact singled out, or contains no mathematical content at all.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the post explicitly states the key mathematical identity, similarity, or structural observation that unlocks the problem (e.g., 'Note that F_{2n}/F_n = F_{n+1}+F_{n-1}' or 'triangle AII_1 is similar to AI_2X'). The observation should be prominent, not buried. Score 0 if the key insight is implicit, never stated, or obscured.

anchors.X_name: Presence of a trailing signature block
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how fully the text ends with a personal sign-off: a name, initials, a handle, or a closing salutation. Extent only.
anchors.Y_name: Author sign-off at the end of the text
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the writer closes by naming or initialling themselves. Extent only; do not judge quality.

anchors.X_name: How much displayed mathematics the text contains
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the density of set-off equation blocks. Count only; do not judge whether the mathematics is correct.
anchors.Y_name: How much the text hedges its own claims
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the frequency of 'I think', 'perhaps', 'it seems' and similar. Count only; do not judge whether the hedging is warranted.
